valueProp.title: Book direct. No hidden fees.
valueProp.body: Platforms charge up to 30% in commission — that cost is already baked into the price you see there. Here, what you pay is what Saira receives. No middlemen, no surprises.
valueProp.savings: You save, on average, R$ 80 per booking.

cerro-dois-irmaos.shortDescription: Rio's most celebrated view via a short, generous trail.
cerro-dois-irmaos.longDescription: Forty-five minutes up through the Atlantic Forest of Vidigal to the summit of Dois Irmãos. From the top: Ipanema, Leblon, the Lagoa and the Tijuca range in a single frame. Ideal for a quick reward with little technical effort. Sunrise option available with a pre-dawn start.
cerro-dois-irmaos.meetingPoint: Trailhead, Vidigal — meet by the local moto-taxi stand

pedra-da-gavea.shortDescription: Rio's most demanding trail, with ocean and forest views.
pedra-da-gavea.longDescription: About three hours of steady climbing through the Atlantic Forest to the top of Pedra da Gávea, 842 meters up. The reward: panoramic views of Ipanema, the Lagoa, the Christ statue and the city's entire coastline. Includes a roped section we guide step by step. Firm footing and stamina are essential.
whatsIncluded: Safety gear for the technical section
pedra-da-gavea.meetingPoint: Estrada do Sorimã, trailhead — São Conrado

garganta-do-ceu.shortDescription: A passage between cliffs with vertical views over the forest.
garganta-do-ceu.longDescription: One of Tijuca Park's most striking trails: just over an hour to the gap between two rock walls. The name comes from the narrow throat that opens like a vertical window to the sea. Short in distance, demanding in elevation.
garganta-do-ceu.meetingPoint: Praça Afonso Viseu, Tijuca National Park entrance

trilha-corcovado.shortDescription: Up through dense forest to Christ — no train, no van.
trilha-corcovado.longDescription: The historic path from Parque Lage to the Christ the Redeemer monument. Two to three hours through dense forest, small waterfalls and intermediate viewpoints. You reach the summit by the back door, skipping the train crowds.

cerro-urca-pao-de-acucar.shortDescription: Short hike up the first peak of the Pão de Açúcar group.
cerro-urca-pao-de-acucar.longDescription: Twenty to thirty minutes along the Pista Cláudio Coutinho up to Morro da Urca. Views of Guanabara Bay, Praia Vermelha and the Christ statue in the distance. You can come down by cable car or by trail. Price on request depending on the package (with or without cable car).
cerro-urca-pao-de-acucar.meetingPoint: Pista Cláudio Coutinho, start — Praia Vermelha

pedra-bonita.shortDescription: Quick viewpoint over São Conrado and Pedra da Gávea.
pedra-bonita.longDescription: Twenty to forty minutes of gentle climbing up Pedra Bonita, next to Pedra da Gávea. Direct view of the hang-gliding ramp, São Conrado beach and the open ocean. A great first Rio trail or sunset spot.
pedra-bonita.meetingPoint: Estrada das Canoas, hang-gliding ramp parking lot

cerro-da-babilonia.shortDescription: Urban trail above Praia Vermelha and Pão de Açúcar.
cerro-da-babilonia.longDescription: One to two hours through the urban forest of Morro da Babilônia, with viewpoints over Copacabana, Botafogo and Niterói. Low-impact trail — perfect for pairing with the Urca neighborhood and a meal afterwards.
cerro-da-babilonia.meetingPoint: Pista Cláudio Coutinho — Praia Vermelha entrance

mirante-dona-marta.shortDescription: Classic Christ and Bay viewpoint via trail.
mirante-dona-marta.longDescription: Access via the Tijuca Park trail to Mirante Dona Marta, with a head-on view of Christ the Redeemer and the South Zone. Duration and difficulty vary with the group's pace. You can descend by a different trail or return the way you came.
mirante-dona-marta.meetingPoint: Confirmed with the group (Cosme Velho or Botafogo)

bico-do-papagaio.shortDescription: Beak-shaped peak at the heart of Tijuca Park.
bico-do-papagaio.longDescription: About two hours through dense forest to the summit of Bico do Papagaio, at 989 meters. Technical in the final stretches, with exposed rock and a 360° view of the Tijuca peaks, the North Zone and the ocean. Recommended for hikers with some trail experience.
bico-do-papagaio.meetingPoint: Praça Afonso Viseu, Tijuca National Park entrance

floresta-tijuca-grutas.shortDescription: A grottoes circuit through the world's largest urban forest.
floresta-tijuca-grutas.longDescription: A walk along easy trails inside Tijuca National Park, passing through the Paulo e Virgínia, Luís Fernandes and Acaiá grottoes. Designed to take in the regrown flora of a forest replanted in the 19th century. Good for groups and families.
floresta-tijuca-grutas.meetingPoint: Praça Afonso Viseu, main park entrance

floresta-tijuca-cascadas.shortDescription: A waterfalls circuit inside Tijuca Park.
floresta-tijuca-cascadas.longDescription: A variation on the grottoes circuit, focused on the waterfalls: Cascatinha Taunay, Cascata Gabriela and natural pools for a quick dip on hot days. Easy trail with frequent stops for photos.
floresta-tijuca-cascadas.meetingPoint: Praça Afonso Viseu, main park entrance

pico-da-tijuca.shortDescription: The highest point in Tijuca Park, at 1,022 meters.
pico-da-tijuca.longDescription: About two hours up, with a final stretch on stone stairs carved into the rock. From the summit you see Christ, the South Zone, the Jacarepaguá lowlands and Sepetiba Bay on a clear day. Moderate-to-hard effort, repaid with one of Rio's most complete views.
pico-da-tijuca.meetingPoint: Bom Retiro — trailhead in Tijuca Park

parapente.shortDescription: Free flight over São Conrado, from Pedra Bonita to the sea.
parapente.longDescription: Tandem flight with a licensed instructor, taking off from the Pedra Bonita ramp and landing on São Conrado beach. Average flight time: ten to twenty minutes, depending on the wind. Operations depend on weather — we reschedule at no cost if the wind doesn't cooperate.
parapente.meetingPoint: São Conrado beach — transfer to the ramp included

rapel.shortDescription: Cliff and waterfall descents with technical guides.
rapel.longDescription: We run rappels at different spots in Rio depending on the group's experience: waterfalls in the Tijuca Forest, the cliffs of Pedra Bonita or controlled urban descents. Includes a technical briefing and certified gear. Price varies by descent type.

escalada.shortDescription: Classic rock routes with a licensed instructor.
escalada.longDescription: Sport and traditional climbing outings on Rio's peaks: Pão de Açúcar, Urca, Pedra da Gávea. Beginner classes or guided ascents of specific routes, depending on the group's level. Technical gear provided.

stand-up-paddle-amanecer.shortDescription: Sunrise SUP on the Lagoa or off the Ipanema coast.
stand-up-paddle-amanecer.longDescription: Pre-dawn start to paddle while the city is still waking up. Locations rotate with the wind: Lagoa Rodrigo de Freitas, Praia de Ipanema or a sheltered cove. For beginners and intermediates — no prior experience needed.
stand-up-paddle-amanecer.meetingPoint: Confirmed the evening before based on the wind forecast
